problem: Behavior-cloned navigation VLAs such as OmniVLA do not act socially or anticipate danger. They avoid pedestrians and matched static objects in the same way (counterfactual accuracy 52.8%, about chance), and their detour strength follows visual saliency rather than whether the obstacle is a person. They also do not slow down before near-collisions. Prior fixes rely on human social annotations or modular VLM reasoning, which weakens the scalability and end-to-end simplicity of VLAs.
motivation: Social navigation needs different behavior around people than around geometrically identical objects, plus early reaction to risk. BC optimizes action reproduction, not social decision making. Linear probes show the base VLA already encodes the missing information: person vs. object is decodable (peaking around Layer 9, decaying toward the output layer), and future collision risk is decodable at ~74% uniformly across depth. The bottleneck is therefore translating representations into actions, not perception, which motivates annotation-free post-training instead of new perception modules.
key_idea: Post-train a navigation VLA with LoRA so it acts on social and danger signals it already encodes: (1) fuse mid-layer features into the action head and train on inpainted person-vs-object counterfactual pairs with a clearance-margin loss; (2) relabel SCAND frames with hindsight future-collision outcomes into a three-tier NORMAL / SLOW+AVOID / STOP target, using EWC to protect the stage-1 social behavior.
insight: Probing localizes where each signal lives, and that dictates the fix. The social signal is most separable at intermediate layers, so it needs an architectural route (mid-layer fusion) plus contrastive behavioral supervision. The danger signal is present everywhere but has no action link, so it needs new supervision (hindsight relabeling). The ablations show the two objectives interfere unless separated. Stage 1 alone gives CF-Acc 96.0 but NC rises 4.9%. Stage 2 alone cuts NC 57.6% but drops CF-Acc to 36. Standard LoRA without mid-layer projection (B0) cuts NC 86.7% but CF-Acc collapses to 41. Adding the projection recovers CF-Acc to 74 without any protection, and EWC, mid-layer freezing and counterfactual EWC bring it to 93, suggesting architectural pathway separation matters more than regularization alone. Graded temporal targets matter: NC reduction is 45.7% with no temporal relabeling, 70.2% with binary labels, and 86.4% with three tiers. The pre-danger tier teaches early deceleration rather than last-moment stopping.
method: Behavioral attribution / probing (diagnostic): contrast-varied pedestrian inpaints show avoidance scales with pixel saliency. Layer-wise linear probes on person/object pairs peak around Layer 9. Probes on hindsight danger labels reach ~74% and are uniform across depth.

Counterfactual data pipeline: YOLOv8 detection + SAM2 segmentation of pedestrians in SCAND, filtered by area, position and relevance to the future path. FLUX.1 Fill Dev inpaints each person as one of 7 static objects (trash can, cone, hydrant, etc.) at the same location. 3,809 frames yield ~26,663 person-object pairs, plus 15,236 appearance-variant pairs (clothing, pose, age, gender).

Stage 1, Social Behavioral Alignment: the action head receives a Layer-9 projection in addition to final-layer features. The loss is L_bc (MSE to GT) + 1.0·L_cf + 3.0·L_sem + 0.3·L_inv. L_cf is a hinge max(0, 0.15 m − (c_person − c_object)) on LiDAR clearance. L_sem is cross-entropy on action tokens. L_inv is MSE between appearance variants. Advantage-conditioned regression uses +1 for person scenes and −1 for object scenes.

Stage 2, Temporal Safety Alignment via hindsight labeling: each frame is labeled by the minimum LiDAR clearance over the next 3 frames (~1 s at 3 Hz). Targets are three-tier: >0.3 m NORMAL (GT trajectory); 0.15–0.3 m SLOW+AVOID (oracle = max-clearance trajectory among 24 rotations of GT plus GT itself, scaled by 0.3); <0.15 m STOP (zero trajectory). Danger frames get 5–10× loss weight.

Capability protection: EWC penalty (λ/2)·Σ F_i(θ_i − θ_i*)² toward the Stage-1 parameters, with diagonal Fisher computed on safe frames. The ablation also adds freezing of the mid-layer projection and a counterfactual-pair EWC term.

Implementation: OmniVLA 7B with frozen backbone; all training via LoRA and action-head weights. The output is 8 relative waypoints (Δx, Δy, cosΔψ, sinΔψ). Inference is single-pass, with no extra modules.

numbers_note: SCAND evaluation is open-loop and offline on an author-defined held-out split (13 bags), not an official benchmark split. Metrics are LiDAR clearance of predicted waypoints: NC counts frames with clearance < 0.6 m, and Goal is a completion ratio vs. human demos (base OmniVLA 108.9%). Several inconsistencies: 'Ours (w/o EWC)' reports Total NC 1,590 in the frame-analysis table vs. 1,593 for B1 'No protection'. 'Originally dangerous' frames (2,460) equal the base model's NC count, although the text says the split is by ground-truth future clearance. The intro's '76% real-world pedestrian clearance' is not backed by any real-robot table, which reports goal reached, collision, steps, smoothness and final distance; the 75.9% clearance gain is on SCAND. The abstract says CF-Acc goes '53% to 93%' (table: 52.8 to 93.0). Real-robot trials are few (n=2–18).
results: On the SCAND held-out split (4,902 frames), SALSA cuts near-collisions from 2,460 to 334 (−86.4%) and raises mean clearance from 0.787 to 1.384 m. It lifts counterfactual accuracy from 52.8% to 93.0% (differential clearance +0.002 to +0.045 m) while keeping 96.7% goal completion. It resolves 90.0% of danger frames with only 3.6% new near-collisions on safe frames, beating NoMaD (84.1% / 4.9%, NC 511). GNM and ViNT look safer than OmniVLA only because they barely move (~8% goal completion). On a Unitree quadruped, SALSA reaches the goal in 80–100% of trials with 0% collisions across Static, Narrow, Pedestrian, Dynamic and Sequential scenarios. The base OmniVLA gets 0–60% success with 20–100% collisions.
limitations: Primary evaluation is open-loop on an offline dataset: LiDAR clearance of predicted waypoints on a self-defined SCAND split, with no closed-loop simulation. The safety metric can be gamed by slower or stopping trajectories, since STOP targets are zero trajectories and goal completion drops from 108.9% to 96.7%.
Real-robot validation is small (2–18 trials per scenario, three to five scenarios, one platform) and compares only against the base OmniVLA. Dense crowds and long-horizon tasks are untested.
Social awareness is measured only as a clearance margin between person and object (the learned differential is just +0.045 m). Yielding, intent anticipation and negotiation are not evaluated.
